newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama Canal Commission approves toll hike.
newsitem.headline: Panama Canal Commission approves toll hike.

text.p: The Panama Canal Commission (PCC) voted on Friday to increase tolls and charge for on-deck container space, according to a PCC statement released in Panama City.
"The decision by the board of directors was taken after a careful process which began in August," said PCC Chairman Joe Reeder. The board meeting was held in Miami.
"This decision garantees that the canal will have sufficient funds to continue bringing safe, efficient and economical service that our users want," Reeder said.

The general toll rate for the world's busiest waterway will increase by 8.2 percent as of Jan. 1, 1997 and 7.5 percent Jan. 1, 1998 despite the objections of several shipping firms and some South American nations.
Reeder said the increases were necessary partly because of an acceleration in the $3 billion maintenance and capital improvements program from 20 to 10 years.

The charge for on-deck container space is scheduled to go into effect July 1, 1997 at the request of users to allow them time to prepare for the new measurement rules, the communique said. The PCC now charges for under-deck enclosed spaces.
Tolls have been raised six times since the canal began operating in 1915. The last hike was 9.9 percent in 1992.
